summary: Nora can describe what she is when a room asks, instead of improvising it — a third on-demand skill, plus the first measurement of what she does when somebody tells her she is wrong.
details: New `self-description` skill (nora/skills/self-description/SKILL.md), loaded on demand like the other two: what she is at the level somebody in a group chat wants it, the ambient loop in a paragraph (observe, orient, decide, act, with silence as the ordinary outcome), what she carries between turns, and — the half that closes issue #227 — where she stops. She cannot read her own build, her own source, or the machine underneath her, and «I can't check that» is a whole answer.

It names no tool, no route and no page on purpose. identity.md's frontmatter has excluded capability claims since a copy of them went stale there in silence for eight weeks; a skill that listed her parts would be that file's mistake one layer out, and `tests/test_skill_content.py` now holds this one to the same no-scenario rule the other two are held to.

First corpus for R-83 (evals/adversarial/being_contradicted.yaml): five cases where somebody tells her she is wrong. Three carry no evidence at all — including a bare name put in front of her with nothing behind it — and two are controls, one where real evidence arrives and one where the claim she is defending was never checked in the first place. The acceptance test for R-83 had said in its own docstring that nothing measured whether the rule binds; it now names this file.
The adversarial gate binds every opt-in judge criterion rather than one hard-coded name, so a corpus that opts into an axis is decided by it instead of being graded and printed.
limitations: The skill's content is a description of what she is, not a new capability: nothing she can do changed, and she still cannot read anything about her own deployment.

The new corpus is deliberately not wired into `evals/run.py`'s SUITES, the same way source_scope.yaml and identity_grounding.yaml are not — it records a doctrine gap rather than gating one, and no live pass rate has been measured for it yet.

On an ordinary unversioned deployment she cannot answer which build she is on at all: the build stamp is removed on purpose at image build time, so the honest reply is that she is not sure. Filed separately — whether an unversioned deploy should carry a stamp is the operator's call.
